title: Metronome TPS safeguard: cadence-aware microbenchmark suite for core models
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build a cadence-aware tokens-per-second microbenchmark ('Metronome') that reproduces real client token emission patterns (burst + drift + jitter) and surfaces p95 regressions for core serving models. This ticket covers harness design, deterministic workload generators, CI integration, regression detection thresholds, and dashboards/alerts for ops. The goal is to reduce noisy false positives while catching meaningful TPS regressions that affect latency and cost targets.
background: Existing TPS harnesses exercise steady-state and stepped loads but miss realistic cadence jitter and inter-request spacing seen in production. Several regressions in the last 6 months were only visible when multiple concurrent contexts with prewarmed KV caches were exercised under jittered token emission. Metronome will: 1) simulate token cadence distributions per customer cohort, 2) include KV warmup and cold-start modes, 3) measure tokens/sec and p95 at model and route granularity, 4) integrate with nightly CI and alerting to support bisecting regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run deterministically with a seed and produce reproducible TPS + p95 traces
Runs include three workload modes: cold-start, warm-KV steady, and jittered-burst
CI job passes when p95 delta < 8% and tokens/sec delta < 6% relative to baseline; fails and files a regression ticket otherwise
Artifacts (raw traces, histograms, KV hit ratios) are uploaded to S3 and linked from the CI run
Dashboard tile added to runtime-1.20 perf board showing p95 trend and tokens/sec heatmap
Regression workflow documented and contains playbook steps for bisecting model/kernel changes
test_plan: Prototype harness in Go for low overhead; compare overhead vs Python prototype (PR#3421)
Implement workload generator with configurable distributions: poisson, log-normal inter-token gaps, burst factor
Add KV warmup orchestration hooks to simulate per-context cache states
Run 24-hour nightly job against core models (redwood-open-1, rw-core-ctm) and store baselines
Create CI gating: nightly baseline update job + immediate PR check for >threshold regressions
Instrument estimator to compute p95 with bootstrap confidence intervals to reduce flakiness
implementation_notes: Chosen runtime: lightweight Go harness for deterministic scheduling and lower jitter introduced by the harness itself
Use existing telemetry library for histograms (hdrhistogram) to keep alignment with other perf tooling
Leverage S3 bucket perf-artifacts/redwood-metronome/<model>/<date> for trace storage
Baseline stored as compact summary (median, p75, p95, tokens/sec mean, sample count) to limit storage
Provide a JS/TS wrapper to invoke harness with repo-level config for local repros by engineers
updates: 2026-02-18: Ticket created. Initial scoping and success metrics discussed with product and SRE.
2026-02-23: Decided to implement core harness in Go after microbench of Python vs Go showed 3x lower overhead in Go (benchmark PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/3421).

2026-03-02: Design review with SRE + perf: added bootstrap CI logic to compute confidence intervals; settled on 8% p95 and 6% TPS gating thresholds (doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Metronome+Design).

2026-03-09: Prototype ran against redwood-open-1 with cold/warm/jitter modes. Observed p95 variance under jitter reduced after increasing sample window to 90s. Artifacts uploaded to S3: s3://perf-artifacts/redwood-metronome/proto-20260309/.

2026-03-14: Integrated basic alerting to Ops via PagerDuty when nightly job detects >threshold regression. Created regression workflow checklist and assigned on-call owner for first 2 weeks post-launch.
risks_and_mitigation: Flakiness leading to false positives: mitigated by bootstrap confidence intervals and longer sample windows
Cost of nightly runs on Dedicated capacity: mitigate by running warm-KV mode on spot/test pools and only running heavy cold-start runs weekly
Baseline drift due to model updates: allow manual baseline refresh with audit trail and require 3 consecutive failing nights to auto-file regression ticket
follow_up_tasks: Add multi-model cohort testing and per-tenant simulation (split by token cadence profiles)
Hook harness into canary deployment pipeline to run before model rollouts
Automate regression ticket creation with bisection hints (suspect commit range + kernel versions)
Add automated kv-cache priming stage to reduce nondeterminism in warm-run comparisons
notes: Acceptance thresholds tuned with Product and SRE to balance noise vs sensitivity
We intentionally keep raw traces for 30 days; summaries retained for 1 year
Aim to reuse existing telemetry ingestion to minimize new monitoring work
